name: RNNLIB
listed_description: RNNLIB is a recurrent neural network library for sequence learning problems.
reason: The szcom fork README (fork of Alex Graves's RNNLIB, built to reproduce handwriting synthesis from arXiv 1308.0850) gives only one timing, 'takes 3 days on Intel Sandybridge CPU', with no baseline library. No speed claim or benchmark in the README, repo page, or WebSearch results; CURRENNT and Theano/Torch comparisons found do not include RNNLIB as a measured winner.

name: SeqAn
listed_description: Algorithms and data structures for the analysis of sequences with the focus on biological data.
reason: No reachable numeric comparison against a named external baseline. Repo READMEs (seqan, seqan3) and CHANGELOGs only say 'Samcat ... faster than samtools' (no numbers), 'Speed-Ups of > 1000x compared to serial execution' (self baseline) and 'performance regression tests'. Leads that were blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED) or only seen as search snippets: Rahn et al. 2018, Bioinformatics 34(20):3437 'Generic accelerated sequence alignment in SeqAn using vectorization and multi-threading' (doi 10.1093/bioinformatics/bty380); AnySeq (arXiv 2002.04561, IPDPSW 2020) reports SeqAn 2.4.0 faster than AnySeq and Parasail for score-only AVX512 and both ahead of Parasail with traceback, no numbers seen; Suzuki and Kasahara, BMC Bioinformatics 2018 doi 10.1186/s12859-018-2014-8 Table 1 lists 'SeqAn ED' 7.97 GCUPS vs Parasail 0.69 and Edlib 13.23 (snippet only, different algorithms, SeqAn not the claimant). Retry from an environment that reaches OUP, BMC, arXiv. SeqAn3 test/performance has no README with comparisons.

name: SLEPc
listed_description: Library for the solution of large, sparse eigenvalue problems.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. gitlab.com/slepc/slepc page has no benchmark text (BSD-2-Clause, description 'Scalable Library for Eigenvalue Problem Computations'); slepc.upv.es is EGRESS_BLOCKED. WebSearch for SLEPc against PARPACK/ARPACK found only the itp2d paper (arXiv 1311.1355; serial wall-time figure, which solver wins not readable) and Yambo/ELPA papers, nothing quantified. Leads: Hernandez, Roman, Vidal TOMS 2005 and the SLEPc technical reports (STR-1 to STR-8), including the parallel Arnoldi vs PARPACK scalability study.
